decisions.reason: It is only lightly featured compared with some peers in the portfolio, but it remained on the site across two years, fits the core laser-marking business, and a large growing firm with slack would usually give such an adjacent product more time rather than drop it quickly.

The product is close to the established offer, had its own page in both years, and supports the firm's single-source coding strategy, so its observed performance appears comfortably above a drop threshold.
Like Product B, it stayed prominently marketed on its own page and extends the firm's established printing technologies, making retention more likely than problemistic reallocation.

As a 2024 launch shown on the home page in a strategic core technology, it is too early and too well aligned with the firm's Industry 4.0 direction for management to withdraw it absent clear failure signals.

The compact laser marking cabin was explicitly launched as new in 2024 and given a dedicated page, so a large innovative firm would normally continue backing it while market feedback is still forming.
Although more specialized, it received an external award and supports the firm's application-specific customization logic, which raises aspirations and makes near-term withdrawal unlikely.
